name: Symmetric alpha-stable laws exist
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.exists_isSymmStable {α c : ℝ} (hα0 : 0 < α) (hα2 : α ≤ 2) (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
  ∃ ν, ExtremeValueTheory.IsSymmStable α c ν
scope_note: 0 < alpha <= 2, c >= 0, where c = 0 gives the point mass at 0, which is not stable.

name: Generalized CLT, symmetric case
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendsto_map_convPow_of_isRegularlyVarying {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hsymm : MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => -x) μ = μ)
  {α : ℝ} (hα0 : 0 < α) (hα2 : α < 2)
  (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ) (-α)) {a : ℕ → ℝ}
  (ha : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n)
  (hna : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑n * ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ (a n)) Filter.atTop (nhds 1)) :
  ∃ ν,
    ExtremeValueTheory.IsSymmStable α (ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableConst α) ↑ν ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun n =>
          ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (a n)⁻¹ * x) (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n),
            ⋯⟩)
        Filter.atTop (nhds ν)
scope_note: Symmetric law only, no centering, no skewness; sufficiency only. See the range-by-range entries and the iff domain-of-attraction-stable.

name: Generalized CLT, 0 < alpha < 1
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendsto_map_convPow_of_isRegularlyVarying_of_lt_one {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {α p : ℝ} (hα0 : 0 < α) (hα1 : α < 1)
  (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ) (-α))
  (hp :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => μ.real (Set.Ioi x) / ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ x) Filter.atTop
      (nhds p))
  {a : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n)
  (hna : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑n * ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ (a n)) Filter.atTop (nhds 1)) :
  ∃ ν,
    ExtremeValueTheory.HasStableCharFun α (ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableConst α)
        ((2 * p - 1) * ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableSkewConst α) ↑ν ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun n =>
          ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (a n)⁻¹ * x) (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n),
            ⋯⟩)
        Filter.atTop (nhds ν)
scope_note: One range of alpha, and sufficiency only; regular variation and tail balance are hypotheses. No skewed instance (p != 1/2) is exhibited in the library.

name: Generalized CLT, 1 < alpha < 2, textbook characteristic function
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendsto_map_convPow_sub_of_isRegularlyVarying_of_one_lt'
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {α p : ℝ} (hα1 : 1 < α)
  (hα2 : α < 2) (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ) (-α))
  (hp :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => μ.real (Set.Ioi x) / ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ x) Filter.atTop
      (nhds p))
  {a : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n)
  (hna : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑n * ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ (a n)) Filter.atTop (nhds 1)) :
  ∃ ν,
    (∀ (t : ℝ),
        MeasureTheory.charFun (↑ν) t =
          Complex.exp
            (-↑(Real.Gamma (1 - α) * Real.cos (Real.pi * α / 2) * |t| ^ α) *
              (1 - ↑((2 * p - 1) * t.sign * Real.tan (Real.pi * α / 2)) * Complex.I))) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun n =>
          ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (a n)⁻¹ * (x - ↑n * ∫ (y : ℝ), y ∂μ))
              (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n),
            ⋯⟩)
        Filter.atTop (nhds ν)
scope_note: One range of alpha, and sufficiency only. No skewed instance (p != 1/2) is exhibited in the library.

name: Generalized CLT, alpha = 1
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendsto_map_convPow_sub_of_isRegularlyVarying_one' {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {p : ℝ}
  (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ) (-1))
  (hp :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => μ.real (Set.Ioi x) / ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ x) Filter.atTop
      (nhds p))
  {a : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n)
  (hna : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑n * ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ (a n)) Filter.atTop (nhds 1)) :
  ∃ ν,
    ExtremeValueTheory.HasStableOneCharFun (Real.pi / 2) (2 * p - 1)
        ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableLogConst ↑ν ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun n =>
          ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.map
              (fun x => (a n)⁻¹ * (x - ↑n * ∫ (y : ℝ) in Set.Icc (-a n) (a n), y ∂μ))
              (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n),
            ⋯⟩)
        Filter.atTop (nhds ν)
scope_note: alpha = 1 only, and sufficiency only, with centering by the truncated mean.

name: Closed form of the constant C_alpha
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableConst_eq_Gamma_mul_cos {α : ℝ} (hα0 : 0 < α) (hα2 : α < 2)
  (hα1 : α ≠ 1) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableConst α = Real.Gamma (1 - α) * Real.cos (Real.pi * α / 2)
scope_note: 0 < alpha < 2, alpha != 1, where the formula makes sense; the value pi/2 at alpha = 1 is a separate lemma.

name: E_alpha = C_alpha tan(pi alpha/2)
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableSkewConst_eq_mul_tan {α : ℝ} (hα0 : 0 < α) (hα2 : α < 2)
  (hα1 : α ≠ 1) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableSkewConst α =
    ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableConst α * Real.tan (Real.pi * α / 2)

name: The drift constant of the 1-stable limit is 1 - gamma
Feller's criterion for the domain of attraction of a stable law
source: Feller §XVII.5 Thm 2; GK §35 Thm 2; EKM Thm 2.2.8
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.domainOfAttraction_isStableIndex_iff {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {α : ℝ} (hα0 : 0 < α) (hα2 : α < 2) :
  (∃ a,
      (∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n) ∧
        ∃ b ν,
          ExtremeValueTheory.IsStableIndex α ↑ν ∧
            Filter.Tendsto
              (fun n =>
                ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (a n)⁻¹ * (x - b n))
                    (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n),
                  ⋯⟩)
              Filter.atTop (nhds ν)) ↔
    ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ) (-α) ∧
      ∃ p,
        0 ≤ p ∧
          p ≤ 1 ∧
            Filter.Tendsto (fun x => μ.real (Set.Ioi x) / ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ x)
              Filter.atTop (nhds p)
scope_note: Both directions, 0 < alpha < 2, general law with arbitrary centering. Uses the library's predicate IsStableIndex; domain-of-attraction-stable is the form with plain IsStable. Normalizing constants are existential in this statement.

name: Feller's criterion with a plain stable limit
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.domainOfAttraction_isStable_iff {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {α : ℝ} (hα0 : 0 < α) (hα2 : α < 2) :
  (∃ a,
      (∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n) ∧
        ∃ b ν,
          ExtremeValueTheory.IsStable ↑ν ∧
            ExtremeValueTheory.stableIndex ↑ν = α ∧
              Filter.Tendsto
                (fun n =>
                  ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (a n)⁻¹ * (x - b n))
                      (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n),
                    ⋯⟩)
                Filter.atTop (nhds ν)) ↔
    ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ) (-α) ∧
      ∃ p,
        0 ≤ p ∧
          p ≤ 1 ∧
            Filter.Tendsto (fun x => μ.real (Set.Ioi x) / ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ x)
              Filter.atTop (nhds p)
scope_note: Both directions, 0 < alpha < 2. The limit's location shift is identified only up to existence.

name: The domain of attraction of the normal law
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.domainOfAttraction_gaussianReal_iff {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] :
  (∃ a,
      (∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n) ∧
        ∃ b m v,
          v ≠ 0 ∧
            Filter.Tendsto
              (fun n =>
                ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (a n)⁻¹ * (x - b n))
                    (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n),
                  ⋯⟩)
              Filter.atTop (nhds ⟨ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal m v, ⋯⟩)) ↔
    (∀ (x : ℝ), μ ≠ MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac x) ∧
      ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.truncSecondMoment μ) 0
scope_note: Both directions. The side condition that the law is not a point mass is necessary and is stated.

name: Every non-degenerate limit of normalized sums is stable
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.isStable_of_tendsto {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n)
  {ν : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure ℝ} (hnd : ∀ (x : ℝ), ↑ν ≠ MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac x)
  (hconv :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n =>
        ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (a n)⁻¹ * (x - b n))
            (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n),
          ⋯⟩)
      Filter.atTop (nhds ν)) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsStable ↑ν

name: The limit in the converse of the generalized CLT, with its characteristic function
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.exists_stable_limit_of_tendsto {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n)
  {ν : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure ℝ} (hnd : ∀ (x : ℝ), ↑ν ≠ MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac x)
  (hconv :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n =>
        ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (a n)⁻¹ * (x - b n))
            (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n),
          ⋯⟩)
      Filter.atTop (nhds ν)) :
  ∃ α,
    0 < α ∧
      α ≤ 2 ∧
        (α < 2 →
          ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ) (-α) ∧
            ∃ cp cm,
              0 ≤ cp ∧
                0 ≤ cm ∧
                  0 < cp + cm ∧
                    (∀ (u : ℝ),
                        0 < u →
                          Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑n * μ.real (Set.Ioi (a n * u))) Filter.atTop
                              (nhds (cp * u ^ (-α))) ∧
                            Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑n * μ.real (Set.Iio (-(a n * u))))
                              Filter.atTop (nhds (cm * u ^ (-α)))) ∧
                      ExtremeValueTheory.IsStableIndex α ↑ν ∧
                        ∃ m,
                          (α ≠ 1 →
                              ExtremeValueTheory.HasStableCharFun α
                                (ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableConst α * (cp + cm))
                                (ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableSkewConst α * (cp - cm))
                                (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => x + m) ↑ν)) ∧
                            (α = 1 →
                              ExtremeValueTheory.HasStableOneCharFun
                                (ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableConst 1 * (cp + cm))
                                (cp - cm) ExtremeValueTheory.StableIntegral.stableLogConst
                                (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => x + m) ↑ν)))
scope_note: The explicit conclusion is for alpha < 2 only; the Gaussian case alpha = 2 is domain-of-attraction-normal. The location shift m is existential.

name: A stable law has a unique index in (0, 2]
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsStable.existsUnique_isStableIndex {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  (h : ExtremeValueTheory.IsStable μ) : ∃! α, ExtremeValueTheory.IsStableIndex α μ

name: Converse of the generalized CLT, symmetric case
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.GCLTConverse.exists_isRegularlyVarying_of_tendsto {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a : ℕ → ℝ}
  (hsymm : MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => -x) μ = μ) (ha : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n)
  {ν : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure ℝ} (hnd : ↑ν ≠ MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac 0)
  (hconv :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n =>
        ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (a n)⁻¹ * x) (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n),
          ⋯⟩)
      Filter.atTop (nhds ν)) :
  ∃ α,
    0 < α ∧
      α ≤ 2 ∧
        ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.truncSecondMoment μ) (2 - α) ∧
          (α < 2 → ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ) (-α))
scope_note: Symmetric law and no centering. The general form is gclt-converse.

name: Converse of the generalized CLT
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.GCLTConverse.exists_isRegularlyVarying_tailBalance_of_tendsto
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a b : ℕ → ℝ}
  (ha : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n) {ν : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure ℝ}
  (hnd : ∀ (x : ℝ), ↑ν ≠ MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac x)
  (hconv :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n =>
        ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (a n)⁻¹ * (x - b n))
            (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n),
          ⋯⟩)
      Filter.atTop (nhds ν)) :
  ∃ α,
    0 < α ∧
      α ≤ 2 ∧
        ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.truncSecondMoment μ) (2 - α) ∧
          (α < 2 →
            ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ) (-α) ∧
              (∃ B > 0,
                  Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑n * ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ (a n)) Filter.atTop
                    (nhds B)) ∧
                ∃ p,
                  0 ≤ p ∧
                    p ≤ 1 ∧
                      Filter.Tendsto (fun x => μ.real (Set.Ioi x) / ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ x)
                        Filter.atTop (nhds p))
scope_note: Necessity of regular variation and tail balance for any centering; the limit is identified by limit-is-stable-explicit.

name: Feller's criterion, symmetric case
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.GCLTConverse.domainOfAttraction_isSymmStable_iff {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {α : ℝ}
  (hsymm : MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => -x) μ = μ) (hα0 : 0 < α) (hα2 : α < 2) :
  (∃ a,
      (∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n) ∧
        ∃ c > 0,
          ∃ ν,
            ExtremeValueTheory.IsSymmStable α c ↑ν ∧
              Filter.Tendsto
                (fun n =>
                  ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (a n)⁻¹ * x)
                      (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n),
                    ⋯⟩)
                Filter.atTop (nhds ν)) ↔
    ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.absTail μ) (-α)
scope_note: Symmetric law and no centering. The general form is domain-of-attraction-stable-index.

name: Lévy's continuity theorem with existence of the limit
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.exists_tendsto_of_tendsto_charFun.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  {μ : ℕ → MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure E} {f : E → ℂ} (hf : ContinuousAt f 0)
  (h :
    ∀ (t : E),
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n => MeasureTheory.charFun (↑(μ n)) t) Filter.atTop (nhds (f t))) :
  ∃ ν, MeasureTheory.charFun ↑ν = f ∧ Filter.Tendsto μ Filter.atTop (nhds ν)
scope_note: On a finite-dimensional real inner product space; sequences. A short proof from Mathlib's tightness and Prokhorov results, but Mathlib does not state the existence of the limit.

name: Characteristic function of the Cauchy law
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.charFun_cauchyMeasure (x₀ : ℝ) (γ : NNReal) (t : ℝ) :
  MeasureTheory.charFun (ProbabilityTheory.cauchyMeasure x₀ γ) t =
    Complex.exp (↑t * ↑x₀ * Complex.I - ↑↑γ * ↑|t|)
scope_note: Nothing left out; gamma = 0 gives the point mass.
